originality.rationale: Qian–Tan–Hong, arXiv:1201.0931v1, explicitly leaves the divisor-sum least-period problem open while proving periodicity and a totient case. Farhi–Kane, arXiv:0808.1507v1, covers the identity quotient but not sigma-alpha, a different multiplicative function with nongeometric prime-power values. A related older identity quotient is excluded from novelty claims. Formula-level implication checks and focused index/literature searches found no known matching divisor-sum theorem; unlocated equivalent later coverage remains a live risk.
residual_risks: A later paper or broad multiplicative-function theorem not recovered through the search could imply the special divisor-sum result.

value.rationale: The explicit question in Qian–Tan–Hong concerns the least period for sigma_alpha. This theorem resolves it for consecutive integers for all k and alpha>=0, while proving a structural local-ratio criterion for a broader non-completely-multiplicative class. It is sharper than a known universal period and is not inferred from the identity-function theorem.
